newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Kamaz sees 97 truck output up 13 pct.
newsitem.headline: Russian Kamaz sees 97 truck output up 13 pct.

text.p: Russian heavy truck maker AO Kamaz KMAZ.RTS expects truck output to rise to 23,500 this year from 20,737 in 1996, the company said in a statement on Tuesday.
It forecast production of the micro-car Oka would rise to 18,000 this year from 8,935 in 1996.
It did not state sales figures but said production value after taxes would rise to 4.57 trillion roubles this year from 3.93 trillion in 1996 and 3.21 trillion in 1995.

Kamaz, located in the autonomous republic of Tatarstan about 700 km east of Moscow, said it expected spare parts production would account for 856 billion roubles of 1997 production value after 455 billion roubles worth last year.
Kamaz shares had risen to $1.46 at 0845 GMT on the Russian Trading System from $1.41 at the close on Monday.
